objective: Learn from literature in the field to propose three candidate research gaps/frontier directions, formulate research questions/hypotheses, and use evidence-grounded LLM analysis to test support, counterevidence, and uncertainty.

corpus.role: pilot corpus, not a representative field-wide sample
corpus.missing_dimension_policy: A zero or absent D01-D10 label in five papers is a normal sample observation; it cannot remove an RQ or establish field-wide absence.

provenance.D01_D02: v1.2 text-only same-session candidate records, with a targeted original-PDF source review for D02
provenance.D03: Not_Analyzed_Out_Of_Scope; excluded from findings and scoring
provenance.D04_D10: v1.0 verified records carried forward unchanged because their operational definitions were not revised; not freshly reviewed in v1.2
provenance.review_independence: No independent Agent B execution or human domain-expert sign-off is claimed.
provenance.formula_policy: No paper-equation transcription, derivation, equation-type comparison, or formula-dependent claim is included.

candidate_directions.title: Detailed in-plant cooling-water process representation within coupled water-power operation
candidate_directions.hypothesis_to_test: Within the five-paper pilot, clear prose describing in-plant cooling-water demand/process as part of a study's own model is less common than generic water-power dependence; author-identified future work may point to remaining modeling opportunities.
supporting_observations: PDF-01 describes a general WSS with desalination, reservoirs, pumps, tanks, pipes, and water-use loads; no cooling-specific process is identified in the reviewed searchable text and model/case pages.
PDF-02 mentions power-plant cooling once in general introduction context; its own model description centers on WDS pumps/tanks and energy flexibility.

PDF-03 models a generic water-supply-to-power-plant dependency and gives cooling as an example, but the text does not describe cooling-specific demand/process variables or control/performance objects.
PDF-05 explicitly lists quantifying power-plant/substation cooling-system dependence on water-supply capacity as future work.
counterevidence_and_boundaries: PDF-04 provides a positive counterexample: its prose describes thermal-generation cooling-water requirements as water-system node demands and describes cooling-water supply/pumping to power plants.
PDF-03 remains a construct-threshold boundary: a generic supply dependency is modeled, but whether that reaches the D02 cooling-specific threshold remains pending user/domain-expert adjudication.
candidate_directions.interpretation: The pilot evidence supports further testing of this candidate direction, not a field-wide claim. No conclusion is made about equation types, detailed thermodynamic fidelity, or prevalence beyond these five papers.

candidate_directions.title: Fast information-layer sensing integrated with slower water/thermal dynamics for early warning or closed-loop control
candidate_directions.hypothesis_to_test: Explicit prose linking fast cyber/information sensing to slower physical dynamics and to early warning/active control is uncommon in the pilot corpus, even where multistage or anticipatory operation appears.
supporting_observations: Carried-forward D04 labels are Not_Addressed in 5/5 pilot papers.
PDF-04 identifies SCADA communication middleware as needed future work rather than a current sensing architecture.

PDF-01 has a day-ahead/real-time scheduling structure, while several papers have proactive or anticipatory labels; the records do not establish the full combination of explicit fast sensing, a slower physical process, and sensing-triggered early warning/closed-loop control.
counterevidence_and_boundaries: PDF-01's multistage scheduling and PDF-02's day-ahead energy-flexibility model are evidence of anticipatory operation in a broader sense; they are not automatically evidence of cyber fast sensing or time-scale-gap-driven control.
The all-Not_Addressed D04 result is confined to these five pilot papers and must not be generalized to the whole field.
candidate_directions.interpretation: The pilot supports keeping 4-1 as a candidate hypothesis and clarifies the construct boundary; it does not verify field-wide absence.

candidate_directions.title: Extending infrastructure service-loss analysis to critical facilities, populations, and social vulnerability
candidate_directions.hypothesis_to_test: The pilot corpus often stops at network performance or facility/region description rather than quantifying population exposure or social vulnerability across the impact chain.
supporting_observations: Carried-forward D07 labels: 2/5 Not_Stated_In_Text, 1/5 Physical_Network_Service_Loss_Only, and 2/5 Critical_Facility_Impact.
Carried-forward D08 labels: 3/5 None_Reported, 1/5 Critical_Facility_Service_Disruption, and 1/5 Named_Case_Region_Impact.
PDF-05 provides a real named-region case and a named water-treatment facility, while its D08 label does not indicate a population-count or social-vulnerability outcome.
counterevidence_and_boundaries: PDF-04 and PDF-05 reach critical-facility/service or named-region levels; these are meaningful intermediate outcomes and must not be described as no human-relevant analysis at all.
A named region or critical facility is not itself a population/social-vulnerability metric. The five-paper pilot cannot establish that the complete impact chain is absent from the field.
candidate_directions.interpretation: The pilot gives a plausible, limited basis to test 5-1 in a wider corpus; it is not a confirmatory field-level gap.

overall_llm_validation_conclusion: The five-paper pilot offers partial, mixed evidence relevant to all three preserved candidate directions. It supports retaining them for broader verification, while identifying counterexamples, one unresolved D02 boundary, and limits to what the current text corpus can establish. The LLM has not conclusively verified field-wide gaps.
limitations: Five PDFs are a pilot sample and are not a representative field-wide census.
D04-D10 were carried forward from v1.0, not reprocessed in v1.2.
The D02 PDF-03 threshold remains unresolved.
No independent human gold standard or independent model execution is available.
The legacy Step 6/7 outputs are historical and contain formula-related analyses; they are not valid as v1.2 conclusions and must not be silently reused.
step7_status: A v1.2 FRDI should use text-only achievement criteria, explicitly include the author-stated cooling-system future work in PDF-05, show sensitivity to the PDF-03 D02 boundary, and remain exploratory.
